meta.title_before: The Field Service Software Category Has

anchor.label: Share of voice
anchor.body: Every brand mention across every question, added up. The five most visible vendors hold less than a fifth of it between them. The remaining 81% is spread across 1,204 other vendors.
anchor.caption: There is no incumbent in the answers. There is a long tail with a logo.

segments.headline: Every question has a winner. Half the time it is not a specialist.
segments.extra_label: The biggest wins that went outside
segments.caption: Of the 49 questions with a dominant answer, only 24 go to a category specialist.

concentration.headline: 49 are settled. 14 are wide open.

segments.name: Settled, one name in 30% of answers or more
Open, under 15% and nobody owns it

ends.label: Most settled
ends.body: A global consultancy takes implementation planning at 92.4%.

ends.label: Most open
ends.body: Multi-site rollout sequencing. The leading name reaches 8.8%.

concentration.caption: The answers are not random. They are just not the same answer twice.

tables.eyebrow: Who the engines name  ·  earned mentions only
tables.headline: The board
tables.caption: Share of voice, on the 88 questions that name no vendor at all. Vendor H appears in 29 of them and wins none. Being in the answer and owning it are different achievements.

tables.eyebrow: What kind of page gets cited
tables.headline: A page with no list is barely in the data.
tables.caption: The list and table rows are the share of 14,880 cited pages carrying that structure. The rest are each format's share of all citations.

tables.headline: A video platform and a trade title out-cite the vendors.
tables.caption: Own-site citations are 5.1% of the total. The other 94.9% is the engines describing this category using somebody else's pages.

tables.headline: The same questions, four different markets.

anchor.body: between the engine that names this category most and the one that names it least, on identical questions over identical days.

tables.caption: Engine 3 cites the most and names the category second least. Volume of sourcing and willingness to name are not the same thing, and treating AI visibility as one number hides both.

question_list.headline: On 8 of them, the leading name is a regulator.

items.text: How do I sequence a multi-site rollout without pausing operations?
What compliance records do I have to keep for subcontracted field work?
How should I price recurring maintenance versus one-off callouts?
What does a realistic first-year total cost of ownership look like?
How do I migrate historical job data without losing the audit trail?

question_list.caption: When a regulator leads, no vendor has published an answer the engines would rather quote, and several draw almost no citations.

gate.headline:
Your category,
measured the same way.
gate.body: Comment the category you sell into. It goes in the queue, runs against all four engines, and the findings become an issue.
gate.method: Method: 88 questions, none naming a vendor, run daily against four AI engines for 30 days. Mention rate is mentions per answer, not the share of answers a vendor appears in.
